sources.title: Darjeeling District: History of Darjeeling
sources.note: Direct official history, paragraphs on Titalia 1817, deed 1835, annexation 1850 and Tumlong 1861. Colonial judgments about empty land, civilization and benevolent rule not adopted; erroneous statement that India became a republic in 1947 excluded.

sources.title: High Court of Sikkim: Judicial History of Sikkim, historical treaty reproductions
sources.note: Full text of court-published museum booklet read through its public digitization. Titalia printed pages 20 to 22; Darjeeling deed 24; Tumlong 25 to 28. Bibliographic title and compiler Yangchen Doma Gyatso verified in front matter. Museum site corroborates institutional provenance. Use treaty clauses, not unreliable adjacent chronology or colonial preamble as neutral explanation.

sources.title: Joseph Dalton Hooker: Himalayan Journals, first published 1854, later 1891 edition
sources.note: Full original public-domain text downloaded as hooker.html and extracted to hooker.txt. Chapters V and VI: late-1840s Lepcha huts, diet, marriage arrangements, smallpox vaccination in Darjeeling area, bamboo vessels. Racial/caste judgments and unsupported disease theories excluded. All editions and both volumes grouped as one work.

sources.title: British Museum: Lepcha basket base, As 1972,Q.154
sources.note: Direct museum catalogue: nineteenth century, bamboo, plaited, light brown/red, 19.8 cm diameter, 55 g; possible Darjeeling or Sikkim origin marked with question marks. Acquisition unknown. Registration number is not production date.

sources.title: G. B. Mainwaring: A Grammar of the Róng (Lepcha) Language (1876)
sources.note: Original PDF downloaded. Printed page 8/PDF page 40 visually verified: Lepcha la+i+ran, Roman li with diacritic, a house. Modern Unicode U+1 C 1 C U+1 C 27 U+1 C 36 matches printed signs; simplified Roman li explicitly labeled. Gender/kinship discussion printed page 25. Speculative prehistoric etymologies, essentialism and colonial claims in preface not adopted.

sources.title: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew: Joseph Hooker the traveller
sources.note: Full institutional account: Lepcha assistants collected and dried plants; 1849 publication, Fitch illustrations, local plant knowledge. Species described as new to European science, not newly known to local communities. Grouped conservatively with other Kew Hooker biography.

sources.title: Jim Endersby for Kew: Imperial botany and the networks of science
sources.note: Full original scholarly institutional essay: survey anxiety, prohibited crossing, November 1849 imprisonment, British threat and territorial penalty. Grouped with Kew traveller article for source limits.

sources.title: Sikkim Ecclesiastical Affairs Department: History of Buddhism in Sikkim
sources.note: Direct institutional history, final paragraphs: 1642 consecration and founding of teaching centres. Religious narrative explicitly attributed as tradition; no supernatural episode asserted as independently dated event.

sources.title: Namgyal Institute of Tibetology: institutional history and collections
sources.note: Direct institutional page: foundation 1958, collection of texts and xylographs, libraries; Sowa-Rigpa department 2018. Used only as explicitly later continuity, not nineteenth-century provision.

sources.title: Alex McKay: The indigenisation of Western medicine in Sikkim (2004)
sources.note: Original Bulletin of Tibetology article indexed text, printed pages 26 and 32. Direct download timed out. Exact-title and URL queries expose schools from 1880s and early resident biomedical physicians after 1888. One limited later-context passage; no full-text access claimed.

sources.title: Sikkim Legislative Assembly: institutional history
sources.note: Official indexed institutional page confirms statehood via Constitution 36th Amendment Act 1975. Used only for later political endpoint, not as a comprehensive account of contested transition.

proposedOverrides.name: Sikkim (Indian princely state)
proposedOverrides.summary: Sikkim’s changing relations with British India, 1815 to 1878.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Distinct card; no alias with neighboring Tibet, Bhutan, Nepal or British India.
batchIdentityNotes.map: One 1815 to 1878 snapshot, bbox 88.041,26.641,88.869,27.979; Gangtok and Darjeeling included. Public warning explains southern overhang after 1835.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: 1817 Titalia; 1835 Darjeeling cession; further annexation 1850; 1861 Tumlong controls. No flat claim that 1815 Sikkim was part of India. 1878 not political extinction; 1975 later endpoint.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Mainwaring 1876 printed page 8: ᰜᰧᰶ, simplified Roman li, house. Original PDF visually checked; letter la, vowel i, sign ran mapped with Unicode standard.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: Hooker’s colonial judgments omitted. Darjeeling medical example explicitly after cession. Basket nineteenth century with uncertain Sikkim/Darjeeling origin; no invented household ownership. Later schools, institute and medical department explicitly dated. No unsupported nineteenth-century toilet system claimed.
